stops.name: Parco dell'Oglio Sud
stops.detail: The park of the South Oglio is a protected natural area established by the Lombardy Region and occupies an area of 12,800 hectares. It develops along the Oglio river shaft: the landscape is strongly characterized by agriculture where the dense water network often marked by shrub bands and rows, interrupts the ordered series of hills. The golenal areas stand out in the countryside for the imposing boscate masses of poplars and for the dense white willow edges that sometimes extend to form real thickets. The river Oglio is characterized by a sinuous stretch of a single channel with well evident meanders and often steep banks to whose foot emerges in summer extensive sandy beaches. At the mouth of the Mella River (the Flood of the Oglio) there is the northern boundary of the Park, whose area is inserted between the provinces of Cremona and Mantua and ends at the confluence of the Oglio in the Po river, near Torre d'Oglio. The previous bridge stretch, from the exit from Lake Iseo, is protected by the Oglio Nord park.
